premise: Conditional on the WRITTEN all-vector theorem in frontier-20261028-hankel-one-vector-range-v1.json SHA256 f9d7a7beeb70612e8a2698e962cbe04b9549ff9e644a33c1a50b4dfd0035bc0e, which remains unreviewed, for every V the subspace span(H,V) is spanned by rank<=2 matrices.
statement_and_proof: EVERY linear subspace E of M4(C) that contains H is spanned by its rank<=2 matrices. Indeed, for each V in E the entire subspace span(H,V) lies in E and, by the premise, has a rank<=2 spanning set. Consequently every V in E belongs to the linear span of rank<=2 matrices belonging to E; taking all V proves the claim. The same holds when H is replaced by any fixed invertible left/right transform.
source_application: For the fresh-public-source 4x4 Johnston-Lovitz symmetric projector sigma_4,4 described in the premise, and ANY positive semidefinite perturbation tau with any coefficient t>0, range(sigma_4,4+t*tau) contains the local-invertible Hankel support. Thus its range is spanned by Schmidt-rank<=2 vectors. This is a generalized-range-criterion obstruction for arbitrary positive perturbations, not merely a single added pure vector. It does NOT imply that the operator is PPT or has Schmidt number<=2, and does not exclude a Schmidt-number witness using finer geometry.
evidence_and_limits: The strengthening is an elementary logical corollary, with no additional computation. It inherits every named geometry import, the stated exact finite checks, and the unreviewed status of the premise. No historical stopped audit or held selected episode is used; no novelty or formal-review claim.
